questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Quality of the University, Toronto's multicultural environment, and the chance to travel around in a country I will most likely not be able to cover in a one week holiday were the key factors in my decision.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I did not find it easy. I actually missed orientation day because I didn't know where to find the information. The University was however helpfull once I knew where to go for information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Since I didn't attend Orientation Day, I did not receive any information, but I got a lot of information from fellow Students at the first day of classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I could choose between different buildings and chose to live in a 2-bedroom apartment as I travelled with one of my fellow students from Copenhagen and we wanted to live in the same apartment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Our apartment had a kitchen - some of the appliances were a bit old but everything worked. The University also had several on campus restaurants and a whole building just for coffee, ice cream, food and groceries as well as a cantine in case you choose one of the meal plans.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
At York University a lot of the students still live at home with their parents due to high rent prices and therefore most of the people living on campus are actually students studying abroad. 

Also the building we stayed in was not in the best condition, but overall it was a great experience to stay on campus as you could easily access the University Gym and take different yoga/pilates classes on campus and watch University Sport such as Volley and Hockey.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very easy to register for classes and the first two weeks you can actually change classes if you feel like changing after joining some of the seminars.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The University website offered a lot of guidance as well as the Student Services.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that most of the classes have attendance requirements. In most classes you have to make a choice between different exam structures - I choose to write a 7,500 words research assignment instead of taking the ordinary 4 hour open book exam, and in other classes you could choose to let your mid term exam count 40% and the final only 60%

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I followed JD Undergraduate courses at the host University. The courses felt easier compared to master's level at KU, mainly because the grade system is so different. 

In my courses the students attending were both 1st, 2nd and 3rd years. 

It took some time to become familiar with the legal terminology and understand the judicial system, but regular class attendance made the transition much easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The classes are much smaller and the classes were often held on Zoom, but besides that it felt very familiar - usually the professor teaching the class and students were free to ask questions during and after classes. The relationship is however a bit more formal.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Legal Drafting 
Legal Practice Dynamics 
Trademarks 
International Business Transactions
Trusts

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Legal Practice Dynamics was a micro course and thus not graded, but it was actually very fun to get to hear how the law works in practice. 

Trusts was a tough course but also fun to follow as it was taught by a Toronto Law Firm and the Partners and Lawyers were very proficient teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to purchase UHIP the university insurance.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Coffee and some food at cafees were much less expensive compared to Copenhagen. However doing groceries were quite the same as in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of university clubs such as running clubs and gym classes.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Use the weekends to travel! It it quite cheap to rent a car, so we visited Niagara Falls a couple of times, Montreal, Ottawa and also went (by plane) to Yukon to see the northern Lights.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Written above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Canadians are very friendly so it is easy to make friends.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just make contact before or after class!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The kindness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to orientation day, be social and travel!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Orientation day!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting great people and travelling around a beautiful country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Tapping into the language and making new friends.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
